Disease: Yellow fever, unspecified. Year: 2026. ISO3: BFA. DON refs: DON2957. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: A condition caused by an infection with yellow fever virus. Confirmation is by detection of IgM anti-yellow fever virus antibodies in a serum sample.

This condition is characterised by fever, chills, headache, myalgia, conjunctival congestion, or relative bradycardia. Severe conditions may also present with increasing fever, jaundice, renal failure, or bleeding. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is by detection of IgM anti-yellow fever virus antibodies in a serum sample.

ISO3: BGD. DON refs: DON2946. ICD: B00-B09. Definition: A disease of the respiratory system, caused by an infection with Morbillivirus. This disease is characterised by a blotchy rash, fever, cough, conjunctivitis, or malaise. This disease may also present with tiny white spots with bluish-white centres inside the mouth. Transmission is by inhalation of infected respiratory secretions, airborne transmission or direct contact. Confirmation is by detection of Morbillivirus RNA or measles-specific IgM antibodies.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Middle East respiratory syndrome. Year: 2025. ISO3: SAU. DON refs: DON2939, DON2918, DON2910. ICD: U00-U49. Definition: A disease caused by an infection with Middle East Respiratory Syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoA). This disease is characterised by severe acute respiratory illness with fever, cough, and shortness of breath. Confirmation is by identification of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome coronavirus from genetic material.

Disease: Yellow fever, unspecified. Year: 2025. ISO3: BOL. DON refs: DON2920. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: A condition caused by an infection with yellow fever virus. This condition is characterised by fever, chills, headache, myalgia, conjunctival congestion, or relative bradycardia. Severe conditions may also present with increasing fever, jaundice, renal failure, or bleeding. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is by detection of IgM anti-yellow fever virus antibodies in a serum sample.

disease: Malaria due to Plasmodium falciparum, unspecified
text: Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Malaria due to Plasmodium falciparum, unspecified. Year: 2024. ISO3: COD. DON refs: DON2899. ICD: B50-B64. Definition: A disease caused by an infection with the protozoan parasite Plasmodium falciparum. This disease is characterised by fever, chills, headache, myalgia, arthralgia, weakness, vomiting, or diarrhoea. This disease may also present with splenomegaly, anaemia, thrombocytopenia, hypoglycaemia, pulmonary or renal dysfunction, or neurologic changes. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is by identification of Plasmodium falciparum in a blood sample.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Yellow fever, unspecified. Year: 2024. ISO3: BFA. DON refs: DON2863. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: A condition caused by an infection with yellow fever virus. This condition is characterised by fever, chills, headache, myalgia, conjunctival congestion, or relative bradycardia. Severe conditions may also present with increasing fever, jaundice, renal failure, or bleeding. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is by detection of IgM anti-yellow fever virus antibodies in a serum sample.

This disease commonly presents with a fever, sore throat, headache, vomiting, or stiffness of the neck and back. This disease may present with an acute onset of flaccid paralysis. Transmission is commonly by the faecal-oral route or direct contact. Confirmation is by identification of poliovirus in a faecal sample or by a lumbar puncture.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Rift Valley fever. Year: 2022. ISO3: MRT. DON refs: DON2773. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: A disease caused by an infection with Rift Valley fever virus. This disease is commonly asymptomatic. This disease may also present with fever, liver abnormalities, weakness, back pain, or dizziness. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is commonly by detection of Rift Valley fever virus specific IgM or IgG antibodies in a blood sample.

disease: Malaria due to Plasmodium falciparum, unspecified
text: Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Malaria due to Plasmodium falciparum, unspecified. Year: 2022. ISO3: PAK. DON refs: DON2771. ICD: B50-B64. Definition: A disease caused by an infection with the protozoan parasite Plasmodium falciparum. This disease is characterised by fever, chills, headache, myalgia, arthralgia, weakness, vomiting, or diarrhoea. This disease may also present with splenomegaly, anaemia, thrombocytopenia, hypoglycaemia, pulmonary or renal dysfunction, or neurologic changes. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is by identification of Plasmodium falciparum in a blood sample.

text: Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Acute poliomyelitis, unspecified. Year: 2022. ISO3: GBR. DON refs: DON2763. ICD: A80-A89. Definition: A disease of the nervous system, caused by human poliovirus. This disease commonly presents with a fever, sore throat, headache, vomiting, or stiffness of the neck and back. This disease may present with an acute onset of flaccid paralysis. Transmission is commonly by the faecal-oral route or direct contact. Confirmation is by identification of poliovirus in a faecal sample or by a lumbar puncture.

Disease: Yellow fever, unspecified. Year: 2022. ISO3: CMR. DON refs: DON2760. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: A condition caused by an infection with yellow fever virus. This condition is characterised by fever, chills, headache, myalgia, conjunctival congestion, or relative bradycardia. Severe conditions may also present with increasing fever, jaundice, renal failure, or bleeding. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is by detection of IgM anti-yellow fever virus antibodies in a serum sample.

Definition: A group of liver diseases characterised by liver inflammation and fibrosis, caused by more than 6 months of infection with one or more of hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus and hepatitis D virus, with or without HIV. Even at stage of cirrhosis there are often no symptoms. Otherwise, clinical features include fatigue, hard liver edge and complications of cirrhosis (muscle wasting, ascites, splenomegaly/portal hypertension). Transmission of hepatitis B and C viruses is by blood and body fluid co

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Acute poliomyelitis, unspecified. Year: 2021. ISO3: AGO. DON refs: DON2682. ICD: A80-A89. Definition: A disease of the nervous system, caused by human poliovirus. This disease commonly presents with a fever, sore throat, headache, vomiting, or stiffness of the neck and back. This disease may present with an acute onset of flaccid paralysis. Transmission is commonly by the faecal-oral route or direct contact. Confirmation is by identification of poliovirus in a faecal sample or by a lumbar puncture.

Disease: Yellow fever, unspecified. Year: 2021. ISO3: CMR. DON refs: DON2710. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: A condition caused by an infection with yellow fever virus. This condition is characterised by fever, chills, headache, myalgia, conjunctival congestion, or relative bradycardia. Severe conditions may also present with increasing fever, jaundice, renal failure, or bleeding. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is by detection of IgM anti-yellow fever virus antibodies in a serum sample.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Measles. Year: 2019. ISO3: ASM. DON refs: DON2583. ICD: B00-B09. Definition: A disease of the respiratory system, caused by an infection with Morbillivirus. This disease is characterised by a blotchy rash, fever, cough, conjunctivitis, or malaise. This disease may also present with tiny white spots with bluish-white centres inside the mouth. Transmission is by inhalation of infected respiratory secretions, airborne transmission or direct contact. Confirmation is by detection of Morbillivirus RNA or measles-specific IgM antibodies.

Disease: Acute poliomyelitis, unspecified. Year: 2019. ISO3: AGO. DON refs: DON2546. ICD: A80-A89. Definition: A disease of the nervous system, caused by human poliovirus. This disease commonly presents with a fever, sore throat, headache, vomiting, or stiffness of the neck and back. This disease may present with an acute onset of flaccid paralysis. Transmission is commonly by the faecal-oral route or direct contact. Confirmation is by identification of poliovirus in a faecal sample or by a lumbar puncture.

Disease: Yellow fever, unspecified. Year: 2019. ISO3: BRA. DON refs: DON2496, DON2515. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: A condition caused by an infection with yellow fever virus. This condition is characterised by fever, chills, headache, myalgia, conjunctival congestion, or relative bradycardia. Severe conditions may also present with increasing fever, jaundice, renal failure, or bleeding. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is by detection of IgM anti-yellow fever virus antibodies in a serum sample.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Yellow fever, unspecified. Year: 2016. ISO3: CHN. DON refs: DON2232, DON2216, DON2219. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: A condition caused by an infection with yellow fever virus. This condition is characterised by fever, chills, headache, myalgia, conjunctival congestion, or relative bradycardia. Severe conditions may also present with increasing fever, jaundice, renal failure, or bleeding. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is by detection of IgM anti-yellow fever virus antibodies in a serum sample.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Rift Valley fever. Year: 2016. ISO3: CHN. DON refs: DON2266. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: A disease caused by an infection with Rift Valley fever virus. This disease is commonly asymptomatic. This disease may also present with fever, liver abnormalities, weakness, back pain, or dizziness. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is commonly by detection of Rift Valley fever virus specific IgM or IgG antibodies in a blood sample.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Zika virus disease. Year: 2016. ISO3: CRI. DON refs: DON2180. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: Zika virus infection is caused by the bite of an infected Aedes mosquito. The most common symptoms of Zika virus infection are mild fever and exanthema (skin rash), usually accompanied by conjunctivitis, muscle or joint pain, and general malaise that begins 2-7 days after the bite of the infected mosquito.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Acute poliomyelitis, unspecified. Year: 2016. ISO3: LAO. DON refs: DON2175, DON2191. ICD: A80-A89. Definition: A disease of the nervous system, caused by human poliovirus. This disease commonly presents with a fever, sore throat, headache, vomiting, or stiffness of the neck and back. This disease may present with an acute onset of flaccid paralysis. Transmission is commonly by the faecal-oral route or direct contact. Confirmation is by identification of poliovirus in a faecal sample or by a lumbar puncture.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Measles. Year: 2015. ISO3: BIH. DON refs: DON2023. ICD: B00-B09. Definition: A disease of the respiratory system, caused by an infection with Morbillivirus. This disease is characterised by a blotchy rash, fever, cough, conjunctivitis, or malaise. This disease may also present with tiny white spots with bluish-white centres inside the mouth. Transmission is by inhalation of infected respiratory secretions, airborne transmission or direct contact. Confirmation is by detection of Morbillivirus RNA or measles-specific IgM antibodies.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Yellow fever, unspecified. Year: 2009. ISO3: SLE. DON refs: DON1341. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: A condition caused by an infection with yellow fever virus. This condition is characterised by fever, chills, headache, myalgia, conjunctival congestion, or relative bradycardia. Severe conditions may also present with increasing fever, jaundice, renal failure, or bleeding. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is by detection of IgM anti-yellow fever virus antibodies in a serum sample.
